summary: Glenn County, CA lookout site on the Mendocino NF; register dates the structure to about 1914 and names Winchester Riffe as lookout 1914-1928; removal date and current status unknown.

facts.design: Unique design with a very narrow window set, per the register; no dimensions given
facts.status_note: Register lists removal as unknown; Peakbagging marks the site '(LO site)', meaning the building has been removed or its status is unknown
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Mendocino National Forest

events.note: Site served as a lookout as early as 1912, with communication by heliograph
Register dates the structure to circa 1914
Register: Winchester Riffe served as lookout from at least 1914
1919 California District News Letter names 'Chess Riffe' as lookout on Black Butte for five years; the sources do not say he is Winchester Riffe
1927 Ukiah Dispatch-Democrat item says 'Chas. Riffe' took up his duties as forest lookout there; not tied to Winchester Riffe
Register's range for Winchester Riffe ends in 1928
1930 Ukiah Republican Press item describes a stone slab bearing Winchester Riffe's name near the station
Register says the original structure may have been replaced in 1936

corrections.why: The register lists removal as unknown and does not say nothing remains. Peakbagging's '(LO site)' code covers a removed building or an unknown status, so 'gone' is not established

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 7,451 ft (2,271 m). A 1928 Dispatch-Democrat item quoted on the weebly page gives 7458 feet. The register figure is used in facts; the difference is not explained.
Newspapers name Riffes at the lookout as 'Chess' (1919) and 'Chas.' (1927), and the register names Winchester Riffe. The sources do not say whether these are one man, so the names are kept separate.

notes_for_editor: Status is unknown, and the lookouts' names differ across newspaper items. Do not use the 2001 'Black Butte lookout tower collapses' article or the 2021 'On the lookout' article from The Nugget (Sisters, Oregon): both concern a different Black Butte near Sisters, Oregon. The brief's 'ground' kind is not confirmed by any source read; the register calls it a 'structure' with a narrow window set. No photos with image URLs were read; the register lists a 2009 'Lookout Site' photo credited to Ron Kemnow, but no image was fetched.
